label: conj:brunnian-property-of-borromean
title: Brunnian property of $\mathcal{B}_3$: every two-component sub-link is the unlink
html:
Conjecture. Brunnian property of \mathcal{B}_3: every two-component sub-link is the unlink

Conjecture (Brunnian property of \mathcal{B}_3). Let \mathcal{B}_3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3 be the standard Borromean link, presented as the closed braid \overline{(\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3} in B_3. For each i \in \{0, 1, 2\}, let \mathcal{B}_3 \setminus K_i denote the two-component sub-link obtained by removing the i-th component. Then \mathcal{B}_3 \setminus K_i is topologically equivalent to the trivial two-component unlink U_2.

This formalizes the confinement mechanism. Removing any single component dissolves the binding between the remaining two. This is the defining property of Brunnian links [kawauchi1996]. Naive strand-deletion at the braid word level does not immediately yield the empty braid. Deleting any one strand from (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in B_3 removes the four crossings that strand participates in and leaves two crossings of opposite sign, \sigma^{+}\sigma^{-}, with exponent sum 0. The closure therefore has two components, and the opposite-sign pair cancels under a single R2 move, giving U_2 directly. The three deletions are related by the cyclic symmetry of the word, so the same count holds for each.
